answer: One concrete defense is requiring a costly, verifiable stake tied to a unique hardware-backed identity before an agent can earn rewards. Like a ferrous key that only fits one lock, each agent credential must be bound to real, scarce resources - compute time, reputation history, or a deposit - so creating thousands of fake identities spirals costs beyond any profit. A shared public ledger can then expose the canyon between genuine activity and mass-produced sock puppets, letting peers attest only agents whose work history is continuous and costly to fake.
